newsitem.title: BELGIUM: TENNIS-LEG PROBLEM AND DAMM SEND RIOS PACKING.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-LEG PROBLEM AND DAMM SEND RIOS PACKING.

text.p: World number six Marcelo Rios of Chile, hampered by a leg injury, slumped to a 4-6 7-5 7-6 defeat by Czech Martin Damm in the second round of the European Community tennis championship but said he would have forfeited the next round anyhow.
"I'm not pleased because I lost. But I don't think I should have played. It was not a good decision to play," second-seeded Rios said.
"I think that if I had won this match I would not have been able to play the next match," he said.
Rios, 21, was forced to pull out of the Marseille final against Swede Thomas Enqvist last week but had come through the first round in Antwerp without mishap.

But Rios, the second seed and highest ranked player in the tournament following the withdrawal of top seed Goran Ivanisevic on Tuesday, was a pale shadow of the player who dominated Romanian Adrian Voinea in the first round.

The Chilean, who had never played Damm before, faded as the match progressed. In the final set he quickly fell 5-2 behind but battled back to level 6-6, more because of Damm's erratic play than through his own performance.
Damm, world number 48, twisted his ankle when leading 6-5 and had it strapped before resuming play.
The decisive tie-break was a sad affair with Rios clearly holding back and the match was sealed 7-3.
"I didn't feel good enough to play well. With every point I was killing my leg," said Rios.
Rios said he would take next week off and travel to the United States to have his leg treated, partly with ultra-sound massage.
